summary: Eight years of marine operations across a ferry deck and a remote lighthouse station: sole keeper of a first-order light with six years without an unplanned outage, 14 coastguard incidents coordinated by radio, four supply landings a year planned end to end. Builds the tools the job lacks — a telemetry logger the Lights Board now schedules its maintenance from.

experience.org: Northern Isles Lights Board, Skerra Head Lighthouse
bullets: Sole keeper of a first-order rotating light and fog signal, on a rota with one relief keeper; six years without an unplanned outage of the light (2018–2024), maintaining the lens drive, lamp changer and standby generator myself.
Coordinated 14 incidents with the coastguard by VHF since 2019, including three helicopter medical evacuations.

Planned and managed four supply landings a year — inventory, ordering and the landing plan agreed with the supply vessel's master — and the station's consumables and spares budget of about £40,000 a year.
Trained five relief keepers and wrote the 40-page station handbook; weather observations every three hours for the national meteorological service.
Deck crew on a 40-metre ro-ro ferry, six crossings a day: mooring, cargo lashing, passenger safety briefings; bosun's mate from 2016, responsible for the deck department's daily checks.
Radio watch on the bridge; GMDSS General Operator's Certificate (2014), STCW basic safety training (2013, renewed 2018).

projects.org: Telemetry for a lighthouse station · personal project
bullets: Raspberry Pi logger in Python recording fog-signal activations and generator running hours, three years of continuous data; the Lights Board's engineering office plans its maintenance visits from the monthly export.
